newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Thousands of Taiwanese protest over rising crime.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Taiwanese protest over rising crime.

text.p: More than 50,000 demonstrators marched on the presidential office on Sunday to protest against Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui's failure to replace the prime minister in response to growing concerns about crime.
In the second major protest this month urging the government to fight rising crime, demonstrators carried placards demanding the immediate sacking of prime minister Lien Cha.
On Thursday Lee accepted the blame for what he called Taiwan's worsening social order and accepted the offer of his hand-picked premier to quit in July, but this has not satisfied the protesters.
When they arrived at the presidential office, which was protected by a heavy police guard, they lay down on the pavement outside, outlined their bodies in chalk and wrote in their demands.
Protesters also flashed laser messages on the wall of the presidential office saying "apologise" and "step down".

"The best way for President Lee to demonstrate his concern is to replace the premier immediately," said Lin Yi-hsiung, spokesman for the protesters and a prominent member of the opposition Democratic Progressive Party.

Lien and his cabinet face fierce criticism over a recent spate of still unsolved violent crimes, including the gangland-style execution of a county magistrate and seven colleagues and the kidnap-murder of the daughter of a prominent actress.
Lien offered to resign in July after completion of constitutional amendments by the National Assembly.
Organisers of the march complained that the president had not offered any concrete proposals addressing the public's concerns about crime.

The size of the crowd exceeded the expectations of the organisers, the Humanistic Educational Foundation, which had estimated some 20,000 would take part. All participants signed an agreement promising the protest would be peaceful.
